report.executive_summary: Independent recomputation confirms A's core result: all four packages clear both gates (quality ≥80, defects ≤5), so WO-04 reduces to measured energy on the shared basis. The verified ladder is P1 6 kWh, P3 14, P2 40, P4 67; margins over the minimum are +8, +34 and +61 kWh (2.33x, 6.67x, 11.17x the minimum). The lowest-energy rule selects P1; the ID tie-break never engages because all readings differ. I audited A's gates, ranking, gaps, ratios and headroom claims against the trusted table; they match, with one phrasing nuance noted. Open questions remain questions, not findings. Ballot: P1.
report.figure_caption: Verification figure: recomputed energy ladder for all four qualifying packages on the shared batch basis, with P1-minimum reference line, consecutive gap callouts, ratios versus minimum and defect-headroom chips.

recommendation.rationale: P1. All four qualify; P1's 6 kWh is lowest, 8 kWh (2.33x level) below runner-up P3 on the identical basis, with 1/5 defects (four of headroom). Fallback: P3 at 14 kWh. P2 and P4 sit at the 5/5 defect ceiling and cost 6.67x/11.17x the minimum.

sections.body: The policy qualifies packages with quality at least 80 and defects at most 5, then minimizes energy, ID as tie-break. Recomputed: quality P4 100, P1 98, P3 89, P2 86 — all above 80; defects P1 1, P3 1, P2 5, P4 5 — all within the ceiling. All four qualify; none is rejected. The energy readings 6, 14, 40, 67 kWh are distinct, so the tie-break never engages and the decision rests on the energy column alone. This matches A without exception.
sections.heading: Gate recheck against the trusted table

sections.body: Recomputed order: P1 6 < P3 14 < P2 40 < P4 67 kWh. Margins over the minimum: +8, +34, +61; consecutive gaps +8, +26, +27. Level ratios versus P1: 2.33x, 6.67x, 11.17x. All readings share one batch, output and load, so no cross-basis correction applies. P2 and P4 trail by 34 and 61 kWh and are unreachable under any admissible re-measurement; P3 is only 8 kWh behind, so the outcome is sensitive to a large measurement error or a new defect finding. A's spacing and ratios are arithmetically correct.
sections.heading: Energy ladder, margins and ratio arithmetic

sections.body: Audited A's summary, gate, ladder, defect and open-question sections claim by claim. Verified: the ladder, +8/+34/+61 margins, consecutive gaps +8/+26/+27, ratios 2.33x/6.67x/11.17x, defect positions (P1/P3 at 1/5, four headroom; P2/P4 at the 5/5 ceiling) and exclusion of unverified cost, delivery, maintenance and reliability. Nuance: '8 kWh (2.33x) below P3' conflates margin with level ratio — the margin is 8 kWh (1.33x); 2.33x is P3's level. No conclusion changes. Fallback logic (P3 next if P1 falls; P2/P4 fragile at zero headroom) is sound.
sections.heading: Claim-by-claim audit of A's brief

sections.body: Verified facts: trusted table values; all four qualify; energy order, margins and ratios as recomputed; defect headroom 4/4/0/0 for P1/P3/P2/P4. Open questions, not findings: (1) measurement uncertainty on the 6 kWh reading is unsupplied; the 8 kWh margin absorbs it only if the combined error stays below 8 kWh, each below half-gap (4 kWh) sufficing; (2) cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified and excluded; (3) persistence of the shared basis into future work is unconfirmed and would force re-measurement; (4) defect stability matters only if a 5/5 candidate becomes a fallback. Nothing supplied overrides measured energy.
